pr_title: drivers: usb: usb_dc_sam0: fix memory leak
pr_body:
The usb_dc_sam0 driver is leaking memory when the usb device is detached
using usb_disable().

When a device is detached, the driver does not reliably deallocate the
descriptor bank memory. Therefore, upon the next attach and configure,
another block of memory is allocated. After several connect /
disconnect sequences, the usb interface becomes unresponsive.

This commit adds a static function to release all memory allocated
to the ep descriptors when usb_dc_detach() is called.  Since detach is
called from usb_disable(), this releases the memory when the
interface is disabled.

Fixes #49177

Signed-off-by: Steven Slupsky <sslupsky@gmail.com>

issue_context.title: usb: sam0: device driver is leaking memory when interface is reset

review_comments: Sorry, I mean could it be that the buffer is not allocated for a descriptor? `bank->ADDR.reg = 0; `

I do not think so.  This is only place I could find where the driver allocates memory (described originally in issue #49177):
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/120df9aa1be6ff41be775646ca789f0e8e5ef5d3/drivers/usb/device/usb_dc_sam0.c#L400-L412

So, it appears these memory allocations are descriptors.
 
If the driver is modified in the future to allocate memory for some other purpose, that could be a problem.  But then again, when the driver is detached and then attached again the interface goes through a complete reset.  So, it would likely be appropriate to deallocate everything at that point anyway.

How I see it, memory is allocated for a endpoint inside usb_dc_ep_configure(), but in usb_dc_release_buffers() you iterate over an array of endpoint descriptors and call k_free() without to check if it was allocated at all. And even if k_free() checks for NULL, there should be a check (or at least comment) before k_free() since the code can change, like in the line 402 in your comment above. My short question that expressed the same was: "Could bank->ADDR.reg be (uintptr_t)NULL?"

That is a good point.  I see now that if k_free() changes down the road and does not check for NULL then it would break this.  So, I will explicitly check for NULL before k_free().  I will also add a comment here and another in usb_dc_ep_configure() where the memory is allocated so any future changes to this driver might consider this issue.

The DC_RESET event method will work at the moment because all existing calls in usb_device.c to usb_dc_ep_enable() also have a call to usb_dc_ep_configure().  However, this breaks if usb_dc_ep_enable() is called without usb_dc_ep_configure().  Strictly speaking, the description for usb_dc_ep_enable() in usb_dc.h is silent about usb_dc_ep_configure().  That would need to be changed to indicate that configure is required anytime an ep is disabled.

I cursory look at the other drivers and there seems to be several that do not check if the ep is already configured.  The set_endpoint() function in usb_device.c checks the return code of ep_configure() so there are likely issues with other drivers regarding the configure / enable / disable process.

IIRC we have an issue open about that, however reconfiguration should not be a big issue, but it should always be checked if an endpoint is already enabled or not.

> One way to address this would be to insert a call to usb_dc_ep_disable() from usb_disable() or to generate a DC_RESET event from usb_disable().

I think usb_disable() is neglected because it is rarely used. There is [foreach_ep(disable_interface_ep); ](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/usb/device/usb_device.c#L1191), you could add it to usb_disable() just after usb_dc_detach().

> There is [foreach_ep(disable_interface_ep); ](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/usb/device/usb_device.c#L1191), you could add it to usb_disable() just after usb_dc_detach().

IIRC, I think there is a scope issue and the foreach_ep macro cannot be used from usb_device.c.  I think the DC_RESET approach avoids having to change the scope of some of the driver functions and the api.
Please follow the link, foreach_ep() is local funciton of usb_device.c
I looked further into your suggestion of foreach_ep() in usb_disable() but was unable to find a solution that worked as well as what I originally proposed.  I suggest we apply the current PR.
